name: Affordance Computation
description: Direct perception of action possibilities in the environment (Gibson, 1979). Brain computes how objects can be acted upon: grasp-ability, climb-ability, etc. Neural substrate unclear; limited direct evidence for this as a primitive computation.
key_references: Gibson, J. J. (1979). The Ecological Approach to Visual Perception. Houghton Mifflin.

Glover, S., & Dixon, P. (2002). Latency adjustments for spatial illusions in grasping: does the brain estimate geometric properties of objects? Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance, 28(2), 396-410.
empirical_evidence: Behavioral evidence: grasping scaled to object size independent of visual illusions (Aglioti et al.). fMRI shows motor areas activated by graspable objects. Single-unit recordings inconclusive. Computationally, affordances may emerge from general sensorimotor learning rather than dedicated primitive. Ecological validity of lab tasks questioned.
